safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 1.55 days

narrative: Material PL1__M596AA54 shows moderate daily demand variability (CV=0.362) with a statistically significant downward trend over the observation window. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.811), ranging from 0.36 to 3.59 working days, making lead-time uncertainty the dominant driver of the safety stock requirement. The current SAP safety stock of 396 units is under-buffered by 679 units relative to the 95% service-level requirement; increasing it to 1,075 units eliminates this gap. Simultaneously, consolidating orders from ~68/year to ~15/year via the EOQ-aligned quantity of 11,980 units cuts total annual inventory costs by 56.4% while remaining well within the 28,814-unit storage limit.
warnings: Decreasing demand trend detected (slope=-4.69 units/day, R²=0.252); revisit mean demand estimate quarterly.
SAP safety stock (396) is significantly below the statistically required level (1,075) for 95% service level.
Data loaded from fallback lists; CSV endpoint was unavailable.

research_insights.selection_rationale: All demand observations are non-zero (100% fill rate), demand is approximately normally distributed, and the EOQ substantially exceeds the MOQ, making a continuous-review fixed-reorder-point / fixed-order-quantity policy the most cost-efficient choice. Periodic review would add unnecessary cycle-stock overhead given the predictable replenishment trigger.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding at 45.3% utilisation (13,055 of 28,814 units). No capacity-driven order reduction was required. If safety stock were to rise above ~16,834 units, a cap would activate, but this is implausible under current demand levels.
